name: RADFAB
situation: Studios and retailers needed production software tied to launch dates that could not move.
obstacle: Conference-floor and campaign systems had to hold up at crowd scale on day one, with no soft launch.
decision: Shipped an on-prem LibSQL leaderboard game for the Fallout launch with Amazon Prime Video and Bethesda, a .NET and Cosmos DB backend for Lionsgate’s SISU, and Kafka-driven asset infrastructure on AWS EKS for CarParts.com.
result: 5,000+ players across CCXP Brazil 2023, CCXP Mexico City 2025 and Gamescom Cologne 2025, a Bronze Clio in 2023, and a 500% increase in asset processing speed.
visualAlt: The Fallout activation on the CCXP show floor: an Amazon Prime and Vault-Tec build with a rock facade and vault door, crowded with attendees.
caveat: RADFAB is my own consultancy, and the work there has always been project-based and outside of my full-time hours. Evenings, weekends, and short engagements between projects. My full-time employers were aware of it and it never conflicted with those roles. The engagements tend to be short and campaign-driven, like the Fallout companion games for Amazon Prime Video and Bethesda, or the Lionsgate SISU campaign, so the timeline reads as continuous even though the actual work came in bursts.
